Score a workflow with nothing to tune on a nested design

Source: R/nested-fit-resamples.R
nested_fit_resamples.Rd

nested_fit_resamples() scores a workflow with nothing to tune on a nested design. Each outer fold fits the workflow on its analysis set and scores it on the rows it held out.

Usage

nested_fit_resamples(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
nested_fit_resamples(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'model_spec'
nested_fit_resamples(
  object,
  preprocessor,
  resamples,
  ...,
  metrics = NULL,
  event_level = "first",
  eval_time = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'workflow'
nested_fit_resamples(
  object,
  resamples,
  ...,
  metrics = NULL,
  event_level = "first",
  eval_time = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A workflows::workflow() with no parameter marked with tune::tune(), or a parsnip model specification given with preprocessor.

...

On the generic, the arguments of the method. On a method, pass control = tune::control_resamples() here to set the control. Name every argument after ....

preprocessor

A formula or recipe, when object is a model specification.

resamples

A nested resampling design from nested_resamples() or rsample::nested_cv().

metrics

A yardstick::metric_set(), or NULL for tune's default set. Every metric is scored on the outer folds. A set that does not suit the model's mode is an error before any fold runs.

event_level

"first" (the default) or "second". It names which level of a two-class outcome is the event. It applies to the outer scoring fit.

eval_time

A numeric vector of evaluation times for a censored regression model, or NULL (the default) to leave the choice to tune. Times that are not numeric, empty, missing, negative or not finite are an error.

Value

A nested_results, as nested_tune_grid() describes. .selected is a zero-column tibble on each completed fold, and .inner_metrics has zero rows. There is no grid attribute.

Details

Use it for a baseline to compare with a tuned workflow. On the same design, the two runs score the same outer folds, so their per-fold metrics join by fold label. tune::fit_resamples() does the same job on a plain set of folds. nested_tune_grid() documents what the loop functions share, such as the design, what the estimate describes, the seeds, failed folds and parallel execution.

A workflow with a tune::tune() marker is an error here, and a workflow with none is an error in the tuning functions.

Fold i is tune::last_fit() of object on resamples$splits[[i]], under the seed in res$.outer_fit_seed[[i]]. Each fold also draws a tuning seed that nothing uses, so the outer-fit seeds match those of a tuned run on the same design.

collect_selections(), collect_inner_metrics() and agreement() return zero rows, and autoplot(type = "parameters") is an error. nested_final_fit() fits the workflow on all the data.

Differences from calling tune directly

A tune::control_resamples() passed through ... as control is kept as extract_procedure(res)$control. The one tune call a fold makes is the outer fit, which runs under its own tune::control_last_fit(). tune::control_grid() and control_last_fit() also carry the control_resamples class, so both are accepted too.

Forced: allow_par. The outer fit runs with allow_par = FALSE, because the outer folds carry the parallelism.

Settable as its own argument: event_level. Set the level with the event_level argument. A control left at the default level, "first", takes the argument's level. A control set to another level than the argument's is an error. eval_time is an argument too.

Refused: none. No setting is refused on its own. A control of another class is an error, even a control_bayes() that tune itself accepts.

Passed through: none. There is no inner tuning call.

Kept from the outer fit: save_pred, extract. With save_pred = TRUE, the result has a .predictions column. With an extract function, it has an .extracts column. Without them, the outer fit's predictions and extracts are still discarded.

Not returned: none. There is no inner run.

Inert: verbose, pkgs, save_workflow, parallel_over, backend_options, workflow_size. Each one sets an inner tuning call that this function never makes. The workflow's packages must still be installed.

See also

nested_tune_grid(), nested_resamples(), nested_final_fit(), tune::fit_resamples()

Examples

data(mtcars)

# A fixed workflow: no tune() marker anywhere.
fixed <- workflows::workflow(mpg ~ ., parsnip::linear_reg())

set.seed(1)
folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2),
  inside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2)
)

set.seed(2)
res <- nested_fit_resamples(fixed, folds)
collect_metrics(res)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err
#>   <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 rmse    standard   5.93      2   2.06 
#> 2 rsq     standard   0.495     2   0.119

# The record says no tuning ran.
extract_procedure(res)$tuner
#> [1] "fit_resamples"
res$.selected[[1]]
#> # A tibble: 0 × 0
